0.1: A computer transforms input into output by executing stored instructions.
Hardware is physical equipment; software is the instructions and data it uses.
The CPU fetches, decodes and executes instructions using registers and execution units.
A core executes instructions; hardware threads share a core's resources.
RAM holds active program data and loses contents when power is removed.
HDDs use spinning disks; SSDs use flash memory with lower access latency.
GPUs execute many similar operations in parallel, useful for large matrix computations.
Binary represents numbers using only digits 0 and 1.
A bit stores one binary digit; a byte normally contains eight bits.
Registers, caches, RAM and storage trade capacity for access speed.
Cache holds recently useful data near a processor to avoid slower reads.
Input/output transfers data between the program and external devices or files.
Source is interpreted or compiled into instructions scheduled by the operating system.
0.2: An operating system manages hardware resources and provides services to applications.
The kernel is the privileged core controlling memory, scheduling and devices.
User space restricts applications; kernel space permits protected hardware operations.
A process is a running program with its own address space.
Threads are execution paths sharing a process's memory and resources.
Processes move through states such as ready, running, waiting and terminated.
Context switching saves one execution state and restores another.
Scheduling chooses which runnable task receives CPU time next.
Memory management allocates, tracks and protects regions used by programs.
Virtual memory maps process addresses to physical memory and possibly disk.
A file system organizes named data and directories on storage.
Environment variables pass string settings from a parent process to a child.
Concurrency lets multiple tasks make progress during overlapping time periods.
Parallelism executes multiple tasks at the same physical instant.
A race occurs when unsynchronized access makes results depend on timing.
A deadlock occurs when tasks wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.
0.3: A network connects devices so they can exchange data using shared protocols.
The internet connects independent networks through routing and packet exchange.
A client requests work from a server that provides a service.
An IP address identifies a network interface for packet delivery.
DNS translates domain names into records such as IP addresses.
A domain is a hierarchical name that makes internet services easier to locate.
A port identifies a transport endpoint on a host.
TCP delivers an ordered byte stream with retransmission and flow control.
UDP sends independent datagrams without guaranteeing delivery or order.
HTTP defines stateless request and response semantics for web communication.
HTTPS is HTTP protected by TLS encryption and server authentication.
Methods such as GET and POST describe the intended request operation.
Status codes classify success, client errors and server errors.
A request sends method, target, headers and optional data; a response returns a result.
TLS authenticates peers and encrypts data while it travels over a connection.
REST organizes interactions around resources using uniform interfaces and stateless requests.
WebSockets maintain a persistent bidirectional connection after an HTTP handshake.
A reverse proxy receives client requests and forwards them to backend services.
0.4: A terminal displays text and sends your input to an interactive program.
A shell interprets commands, launches programs and connects their input and output.
Files contain named data; directories organize names into a hierarchy.
Commands such as pwd, ls and cd inspect and change your current location.
File operations change directory entries or contents; practice them on disposable data.
Permissions define which users may read, write or execute a resource.
Users identify accounts; groups collect accounts for shared access control.
Signals notify processes about events such as termination or interruption.
Package managers install, upgrade and remove software with dependency information.
Bash interprets shell commands and supports variables, conditions, loops and functions.
Environment variables provide inherited configuration such as PATH to launched programs.
SSH provides authenticated, encrypted remote command execution.
Logs record events that help reconstruct what a program did.
A shell script stores commands so a workflow can be repeated.
0.5: Version control records file changes so revisions can be compared and restored.
Installing Git provides a local command-line tool for managing repository history.
A repository stores project history, objects and references.
The working tree is the set of checked-out files you can edit.
Staging selects the exact changes that the next commit will record.
A commit records a snapshot with metadata and links to parent commits.
A branch is a movable reference to a line of commits.
Merging combines histories and attempts to reconcile their file changes.
A conflict needs manual resolution when Git cannot safely combine edits.
A pull request proposes branch changes and provides a place for review.
A .gitignore file specifies untracked paths Git should normally ignore.
A README explains a project's purpose, setup, usage and verification.
GitHub supports shared repositories, issues, reviews and protected collaboration workflows.
Tags name specific commits, often to identify a released version.
1.1: Install Python and verify the executable and version used by your shell.
The interpreter reads and executes Python code using runtime objects.
An IDE combines editing, navigation and debugging; select the correct Python environment.
A variable is a name bound to an object, not a typed storage box.
A data type determines a value's supported operations and behavior.
Python provides integers, floating-point numbers and other numeric types with different precision.
Strings are immutable sequences of Unicode characters.
Booleans represent True and False and participate in logical conditions.
Operators perform actions such as arithmetic, comparison and membership tests.
Type conversion constructs a value of another type and may fail.
input reads a line as text, which must be validated before conversion.
Formatted string literals insert expressions into readable output.
Conditions choose which code runs based on truth-valued expressions.
if starts a condition, elif adds alternatives, and else handles the remaining case.
A for loop visits items supplied by an iterable.
A while loop repeats while its condition remains true.
Nested loops place iteration inside iteration, often multiplying the work performed.
break exits a loop; continue skips to its next iteration.
String methods return transformed text or information without modifying the original string.
Lists are ordered, mutable sequences that may contain mixed object types.
Tuples are ordered, immutable sequences useful for fixed groups of values.
Sets store unique hashable items and support membership and set operations.
Dictionaries map unique hashable keys to values with efficient lookup.
Mutable objects can change in place; immutable values require replacement objects.
1.2: A def statement creates a named function with parameters and a body.
Calling a function evaluates arguments and executes its body.
Parameters are the names in a function's definition.
Arguments are the actual values supplied when calling a function.
return ends a function and sends a value to its caller.
Default parameters supply values when callers omit arguments; avoid mutable defaults.
Keyword arguments bind values to parameters by name.
Positional arguments bind values according to their order.
A starred parameter collects extra positional arguments into a tuple.
A double-starred parameter collects extra keyword arguments into a dictionary.
A lambda creates a small anonymous function containing one expression.
Scope determines where a name can be resolved.
Local names belong to a function; global names belong to its module.
Recursion solves a problem through smaller self-calls and requires a base case.
A module is an importable Python file or module object.
A package groups related modules into an importable namespace.
The import system finds, loads and caches modules using search paths.
Reusable code expresses one responsibility behind a stable, documented interface.
Modular structure groups related behavior and limits dependencies between parts.
1.3: OOP organizes programs around objects that combine state and behavior.
A class defines the structure and behavior of its instances.
An object is a runtime instance with identity, type and state.
Attributes are named values accessed through an object or class.
Methods are functions attached to classes that operate on instances or classes.
Initialization configures a new instance, commonly through __init__ in Python.
self conventionally names the instance received by an instance method.
Instance variables store state specific to one object.
Class variables live on the class and can be shared across instances.
Encapsulation hides implementation details behind a deliberate public interface.
Inheritance derives behavior from a parent class and creates an is-a relationship.
Polymorphism lets different objects satisfy the same expected interface.
Abstraction exposes essential behavior while hiding implementation details.
Composition builds behavior by combining collaborating objects.
Overriding replaces inherited method behavior in a subclass.
A class method receives the class as its first argument.
A static method belongs to a class namespace without receiving an implicit instance.
Properties expose controlled getter and setter behavior through attribute syntax.
Dunder methods connect custom classes to Python protocols such as iteration.
1.4: Exceptions signal failure; try, except and finally define recovery and cleanup.
Custom exception classes distinguish meaningful failure types in your application.
File handling opens, reads, writes and closes persistent byte or text streams.
JSON processing converts between a text interchange format and program values.
CSV processing reads and writes tabular text while handling quoting and delimiters.
A list comprehension constructs a list from an iterable and optional filter.
A dictionary comprehension constructs key-value pairs from an iterable.
A set comprehension constructs unique values from an iterable.
An iterator yields one item at a time and signals when exhausted.
A generator suspends execution at yield and resumes when requested.
A decorator wraps or transforms a function while preserving its callable role.
A context manager defines enter and exit behavior around a resource's lifetime.
with invokes a context manager and guarantees its exit logic after the block.
Type hints describe expected types for tools without automatically enforcing them at runtime.
Dataclasses generate common methods for classes that primarily hold data.
Enums define a fixed set of named values.
Regular expressions match text patterns rather than general programming syntax.
A virtual environment isolates a project's Python dependencies.
pip installs Python distributions from indexes or other supported sources.
Dependency management records required versions and resolves compatible packages.
Packaging defines metadata and build configuration for distributing Python projects.
Async programming coordinates tasks that may suspend while waiting.
async defines a coroutine; await suspends it until awaited work is ready.
Async I/O overlaps waits for networks or files without requiring one thread per wait.
Debugging inspects execution state to find the cause of incorrect behavior.
Logging records structured events at meaningful severity levels.
1.5: PEP 8 describes style conventions that improve consistency in Python code.
Clean code makes intent explicit through small responsibilities and readable structure.
Names should communicate purpose and follow a consistent local convention.
A type checker analyzes annotations to find incompatible operations before execution.
Static analysis inspects code without running its normal behavior.
A formatter applies deterministic layout rules to source code.
A linter reports suspicious patterns and style or correctness issues.
Debugging techniques include breakpoints, minimal reproductions and checking assumptions.
Unit tests verify a small unit's observable behavior with controlled dependencies.
Pytest discovers test functions and supplies assertions, fixtures and parametrization.
Fixtures provide reusable setup and teardown for tests.
Mocks replace external dependencies so a test can control interactions and failures.
Documentation explains interfaces, assumptions, examples and limitations.
Profiling measures time or memory consumption to locate actual bottlenecks.
Performance awareness considers complexity and resource limits before premature optimization.
1.6-javascript: JavaScript uses dynamic values, functions and an event loop to build interactive programs.
Variables bind values; functions encapsulate behavior and may form closures.
Arrays store ordered values; objects group named properties.
ES modules expose and import explicitly named bindings across files.
A promise represents a future result that can fulfill or reject.
async functions return promises; await pauses their continuation until settlement.
fetch makes HTTP requests and returns a promise; HTTP errors need explicit status checks.
TypeScript types statically describe allowed values and operations.
Interfaces describe object contracts that compatible values can satisfy.
Generics express reusable relationships between input and output types.
Narrowing refines a union using runtime checks or control flow.
Typed API calls pair static contracts with runtime validation of untrusted responses.
1.6-sql: A database persists data and provides controlled querying and updates.
Tables organize rows under named, typed columns.
Column types define valid representations and influence comparison and storage.
SELECT retrieves expressions and rows from relations.
INSERT adds new rows subject to constraints.
UPDATE changes matching rows; a missing predicate may affect every row.
DELETE removes matching rows and should use a deliberate predicate.
WHERE filters individual rows before grouping.
GROUP BY collects rows into groups for aggregation.
JOIN combines rows according to relationships or matching predicates.
A subquery places one query inside another query.
Aggregates such as COUNT and SUM summarize multiple rows.
Constraints reject invalid rows or relationships at the database boundary.
An index accelerates selected lookups while adding storage and write cost.
1.6-bash: A shell parses command text, expands values and launches processes.
Shell variables bind strings; quote expansions to preserve spaces and special characters.
Conditions choose commands using exit statuses and test expressions.
Loops repeat commands over items or while a condition succeeds.
Shell functions group commands into reusable named operations.
Exported variables become part of a child process's environment.
Scripts require an appropriate interpreter and permissions; inspect their exit status.
2.1: Number systems represent quantities using chosen digits and place values.
A fraction represents a ratio of integers with a nonzero denominator.
Decimals express numbers using powers of ten.
A percentage is a ratio expressed per hundred.
A ratio compares quantities through division.
A power is the result of raising a base to an exponent.
An exponent specifies repeated multiplication or its generalized extension.
A root reverses exponentiation, such as a square root reversing squaring.
A logarithm answers which exponent produces a given value from a base.
An algebraic expression combines constants, variables and operations.
A linear equation contains variables only to the first power.
A quadratic equation includes a squared variable and may have two real roots.
A mathematical function assigns exactly one output to each allowed input.
Domain lists allowed inputs; range lists outputs actually produced.
A graph visually represents relationships between variables or objects.
Coordinate geometry represents positions and shapes using numerical coordinates.
2.2: Propositional logic studies statements with truth values and their combinations.
Logical operators combine or negate truth-valued statements.
A truth table enumerates every input combination and its logical output.
A set is an unordered collection of distinct elements.
Union, intersection and difference combine sets by membership rules.
A relation specifies which ordered pairs of elements are connected.
A function is a relation assigning one output to each input.
Permutations count arrangements in which order matters.
Combinations count selections in which order does not matter.
Counting principles combine counts through addition or multiplication under stated conditions.
Induction proves a base case and a step from one integer to the next.
Graph theory studies vertices and the edges connecting them.
Nodes represent entities; edges represent connections or relationships.
A tree is a connected graph without cycles.
Boolean algebra expresses and transforms rules over true and false values.
2.3: A population is the full group of interest; a sample is an observed subset.
The mean is the sum of observations divided by their count.
The median is the middle value after sorting observations.
The mode is the most frequently occurring value.
The range is the difference between maximum and minimum observations.
Variance measures average squared deviation from the mean using the appropriate denominator.
Standard deviation is the square root of variance, in the original units.
A percentile is a threshold below which a chosen percentage of observations falls.
Quartiles divide ordered observations into four approximately equal groups.
A distribution describes possible values and their frequencies or probabilities.
A normal distribution is a symmetric bell-shaped family defined by mean and variance.
Skewness describes asymmetry in a distribution.
An outlier is unusually far from the typical observations under a chosen rule.
Correlation measures association and does not establish a causal relationship.
Covariance measures how two variables vary together, with units tied to both.
Sampling methods determine how observations are selected and what biases may arise.
Inference uses sample evidence to estimate or test claims about a population.
A confidence interval comes from a procedure with stated long-run coverage.
A hypothesis test compares data with a specified null model.
A p-value measures tail probability under a null model, not the probability the null is true.
2.4: Probability assigns values between zero and one to uncertain events.
An event is a set of outcomes in a probability space.
Independent events do not change each other's probability.
Conditional probability measures an event's probability given another event has occurred.
Bayes' theorem computes a posterior from prior probability and evidence likelihood.
A random variable maps outcomes to numerical values.
A discrete distribution assigns probabilities to countable values.
A continuous distribution uses a density over a continuum of values.
Expected value is a probability-weighted average, when it exists.
Variance measures expected squared distance from a random variable's mean.
A density integrates over a region to give probability; its value is not itself a point probability.
Bernoulli, binomial and normal distributions model different classes of uncertain outcomes.
2.5: A scalar is a single numerical value.
A vector is an ordered collection of numbers representing a point or direction.
Vector operations include addition, scaling and inner products with compatible shapes.
The dot product sums elementwise products of two equal-length vectors.
Magnitude measures vector length, commonly using the Euclidean norm.
A matrix is a rectangular array representing data or a linear map.
Matrix addition combines corresponding entries of equal-shaped matrices.
Matrix multiplication composes compatible linear maps through row-column dot products.
Transpose exchanges matrix rows and columns.
An identity matrix leaves compatible vectors unchanged under multiplication.
An inverse reverses a square matrix's transformation when that matrix is invertible.
A linear transformation preserves addition and scalar multiplication.
An eigenvalue is the scale applied to an associated nonzero eigenvector.
An eigenvector keeps its direction under a linear transformation.
A vector space supports addition and scalar multiplication under consistent axioms.
Dimensionality counts coordinates or independent directions in a representation.
2.6: A limit describes a function's approaching value near a chosen input.
Continuity means the function's value agrees with its limit at a point.
A derivative measures a function's local rate of change.
Derivative rules simplify differentiation of sums, products and other compositions.
The chain rule differentiates a composition by multiplying appropriate derivatives.
A partial derivative changes one variable while holding others fixed.
A gradient is the vector of partial derivatives of a scalar function.
Gradient descent updates parameters opposite the gradient to reduce an objective.
The learning rate scales the size of each optimization update.
Loss minimization chooses parameters that reduce a defined prediction penalty.
Optimization seeks good solutions under an objective and possible constraints.
A local minimum is best nearby; a global minimum is best over the domain.
A multivariable function depends on more than one input coordinate.
2.7: Information quantifies the surprise of an outcome under an assumed probability model.
Entropy is the expected information content of a random variable.
Conditional entropy measures remaining uncertainty after observing another variable.
Cross-entropy measures average negative log probability assigned to true outcomes.
KL divergence measures a directed difference between distributions and is not a symmetric distance.
Mutual information measures how much observing one variable reduces uncertainty about another.
Language models minimize next-token cross-entropy to improve probability assigned to observed text.
2.8: An algorithm is a finite, precise sequence of steps solving a defined problem.
Time complexity describes how operation count grows with input size.
Space complexity describes how memory requirements grow with input size.
Big O gives an asymptotic upper bound, often for worst-case growth.
Arrays store indexed sequences, usually allowing efficient positional access.
Strings are sequences of characters used to represent and process text.
A linked list connects nodes through references rather than contiguous positions.
A stack removes the most recently added item first.
A queue removes the earliest added item first.
A hash map associates keys with values through a hash-based index.
A hash set stores unique keys with fast expected membership checks.
Searching finds whether and where a target exists in a collection.
Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search space.
Sorting algorithms arrange values according to a defined ordering.
Recursion solves smaller instances using self-calls and explicit base cases.
A tree organizes nodes through parent-child relationships without cycles.
A binary search tree orders subtrees around each node's key.
A heap maintains a partial order that makes a minimum or maximum quickly accessible.
A graph represents arbitrary connections between vertices.
Breadth-first search explores a graph by increasing distance from a start node.
Depth-first search follows one path before backtracking.
Shortest-path algorithms minimize path cost under assumptions about edge weights.
A greedy algorithm makes a locally favorable choice at each step.
Dynamic programming reuses solutions to overlapping subproblems.
Optimization improves an algorithm while preserving correctness and measuring trade-offs.
3.1: The software lifecycle includes requirements, design, implementation, verification, release and maintenance.
Requirement analysis translates user needs into specific, testable expectations.
Functional requirements describe what the system must do.
Non-functional requirements describe qualities such as latency, availability and security.
Modular design groups behavior behind explicit, limited interfaces.
Separation of concerns gives different responsibilities distinct implementation boundaries.
DRY avoids duplicating knowledge that would otherwise need coordinated changes.
SOLID groups principles for controlling responsibilities and dependencies in object-oriented design.
Clean architecture keeps core application rules independent of delivery and storage details.
Design patterns name recurring solutions to common structural problems.
Dependency management records, resolves and updates the external code a project uses.
Code review checks correctness, clarity, maintainability and risk before merging.
Refactoring improves internal structure without intentionally changing observable behavior.
Technical documentation records interfaces, decisions, setup and operational procedures.
Error handling distinguishes failures and defines useful recovery or reporting.
Logging records relevant execution events with context and severity.
A testing strategy allocates checks across units, integrations and critical journeys.
Maintainability is the ease of understanding and safely changing software over time.
3.2: Relational databases store structured records in tables connected by keys.
PostgreSQL setup creates a server, database roles and a working client connection.
Database creation establishes a logical container owned by a role.
Tables define rows through named columns and constraints.
Data types govern valid column values and supported operations.
A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be null.
A foreign key requires a referenced row to exist.
Constraints enforce validity such as uniqueness, nullability and allowed ranges.
Relationships describe how records in different tables connect.
A one-to-one relationship allows at most one corresponding record on either side.
A one-to-many relationship lets one parent connect to multiple child records.
A join table represents many-to-many relationships between two entity sets.
SQL queries retrieve or modify rows using declarative expressions.
Joins combine records according to matching predicates and chosen inclusion rules.
Aggregation summarizes rows with operations such as counting and summing.
Subqueries embed a query inside another statement.
A view exposes a stored query as a virtual relation.
Indexes accelerate selected access paths while adding write and storage overhead.
An execution plan shows the operations the planner expects to use.
Query optimization improves execution through measurement, indexing and query or schema changes.
Normalization reduces update anomalies by separating facts according to dependencies.
A transaction groups operations into a unit that commits or rolls back.
ACID means atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.
Isolation levels define which concurrent effects a transaction may observe.
A database deadlock is a cycle of transactions waiting for each other's locks.
Connection pooling reuses a bounded set of database connections.
Migrations version deliberate schema changes so environments can be updated reproducibly.
Backups preserve recoverable data; restoration tests whether recovery actually works.
3.3: Relational and NoSQL systems offer different models, query capabilities and consistency choices.
Document databases store structured documents, commonly with flexible nested fields.
Key-value databases retrieve values primarily through unique keys.
Wide-column databases organize sparse data for large distributed access patterns.
Graph databases store relationships as first-class connections between entities.
Data modeling chooses representations based on facts, relationships and access patterns.
Query trade-offs compare read performance, write cost, flexibility and consistency.
Database selection starts with required queries, correctness, scale and operating constraints.
3.4: Data engineering builds reliable systems for collecting and preparing usable data.
A data source is the original system, file or stream producing records.
Ingestion transfers data from a source into a processing or storage system.
Structured data follows an explicit tabular or similarly rigid schema.
Semi-structured data includes organizing markers without one fixed table layout.
Unstructured data includes text, images or audio requiring interpretation.
CSV represents table rows as delimited text with quoting rules.
JSON represents nested values through objects, arrays and primitive types.
Parquet is a column-oriented file format useful for analytical storage.
Data cleaning corrects or identifies inconsistent, missing or invalid observations.
Validation checks data against explicit structural and semantic rules.
ETL extracts data, transforms it, then loads the transformed result.
ELT loads extracted data before transforming it within the destination platform.
A pipeline connects repeatable stages of movement and transformation.
Batch processing handles a bounded collection of records together.
Stream processing handles events incrementally as they arrive.
Data quality includes accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness and validity.
A warehouse organizes integrated data for analytical queries.
A data lake stores varied raw or processed data for later use.
Lineage records where data came from and how it was transformed.
Versioning identifies reproducible snapshots of data.
Pipeline failures include unavailable sources, invalid schemas and partial writes.
Monitoring tracks freshness, counts, failures and processing delay.
Spark distributes processing across workers; learn it only when data scale justifies it.
3.5: Relational modeling separates entities and connects them through constrained keys.
Document modeling groups data into documents based on access patterns.
Embedding storage preserves vectors together with model version and source metadata.
Vector indexes trade query speed, memory and approximation quality.
Similarity search ranks items using a chosen representation and distance measure.
Metadata filters restrict candidates using attributes such as tenant or document type.
Hybrid retrieval combines lexical matches with vector similarity.
Data access control checks who may read or change a resource.

4.1: AI is the broad field; ML learns from data; data science uses data to answer questions.
A data-science workflow frames a question, prepares data, analyzes it and communicates limits.
NumPy provides efficient numerical arrays and vectorized operations.

Array operations compute over elements, axes or compatible broadcast dimensions.
Vectorization replaces Python-level element loops with optimized array operations.

4.2: Machine learning estimates patterns from examples to make predictions or decisions.
Learning adjusts parameters to improve an objective on observed examples.
Supervised learning trains using examples with known target labels.
Unsupervised learning seeks structure without labeled targets.

Features are input variables available to a predictive model.
Labels are the target outcomes used for supervised training.
Training data is used to fit model parameters.
Validation data guides model choices without serving as the final assessment.
Test data estimates final performance after modeling decisions are fixed.
Training adjusts parameters; inference applies the fitted model to inputs.

Generalization is useful performance on previously unseen examples.

4.3: Linear regression predicts a numeric target through a weighted sum of features.
Logistic regression models class probability using a linear score and logistic link.
KNN predicts from the labels or values of nearby training examples.
A decision tree partitions feature space through branching rules.
A random forest averages many randomized decision trees to reduce variance.
SVMs learn a separating boundary with a large margin, optionally using kernels.
Naive Bayes applies Bayes' theorem with conditional-independence assumptions.
Gradient boosting adds models sequentially to reduce errors of the current ensemble.

4.4: Clustering groups observations according to a chosen similarity notion.
K-Means minimizes within-cluster squared distance to a fixed number of centroids.
Hierarchical clustering builds nested groups by repeatedly merging or splitting clusters.
DBSCAN finds density-connected groups and can label isolated points as noise.
PCA finds orthogonal directions explaining the greatest variance in centered data.
Dimensionality reduction creates fewer coordinates while retaining selected structure.
Anomaly detection identifies observations unusual relative to an assumed normal pattern.
4.5: Accuracy is the fraction of predictions that match the true class.
Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive.
Recall is the fraction of actual positives correctly retrieved.
F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
A confusion matrix counts true and predicted class combinations.
An ROC curve plots true-positive rate against false-positive rate across thresholds.
ROC AUC measures ranking performance across thresholds and needs contextual interpretation.
Cross-validation repeats fitting and validation across controlled data splits.
Regression metrics quantify differences between numerical predictions and targets.
MAE averages absolute prediction errors in the target's units.
MSE averages squared errors and penalizes large errors strongly.
RMSE is the square root of MSE, in the target's units.
R-squared compares squared error against a mean-target baseline and may be negative.
Class imbalance means some outcomes are much less frequent than others.
Threshold selection converts scores to decisions according to error costs.
Calibration compares predicted probabilities with observed outcome frequencies.
Error analysis examines failed cases and subgroup patterns to guide improvements.
4.6: Feature engineering creates representations that make relevant patterns easier to learn.
Feature selection removes inputs according to justified relevance and validation.
Preprocessing prepares input consistently through cleaning, encoding and transformation.
Scaling changes feature magnitudes using training-fitted statistics.
Categorical encoding converts discrete values into numerical representations.
Hyperparameters configure learning behavior rather than being directly fitted as model weights.
Tuning compares configurations using validation while preserving an untouched test set.
Grid search evaluates all combinations in a specified parameter grid.
Random search samples configurations from defined parameter distributions.
Model comparison requires the same task, splits, metrics and evaluation conditions.
Reproducibility records code, data versions, seeds, dependencies and configurations.
Saving a model serializes parameters and required preprocessing for later inference.
Inference runs the saved model on compatible new inputs.
Deployment packages prediction behavior behind a usable, monitored interface.
5.1: Deep learning learns layered representations using neural networks.
A neural network composes parameterized transformations and nonlinear activations.
An artificial neuron combines weighted inputs with a bias and activation.
The input layer receives features in the expected shape.
Hidden layers create intermediate learned representations.
The output layer produces task-specific scores, probabilities or numerical predictions.
Weights scale connections and are adjusted through training.
Biases shift activations independently of input values.
An activation introduces nonlinear behavior between linear transformations.
ReLU returns zero for negative inputs and the input for positive inputs.
Sigmoid maps a real score to a value between zero and one.
Softmax converts a score vector into a normalized categorical probability distribution.
A loss function measures the penalty for predictions relative to targets.
Forward propagation computes predictions by passing input through network layers.
Backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute parameter gradients efficiently.
Gradient descent updates parameters in the direction of decreasing loss.
An optimizer defines how gradients and state determine parameter updates.
An epoch is one pass through the training dataset.
A batch is a group of examples processed in one training step.
The learning rate sets the scale of optimizer updates.
Regularization discourages overly complex or unstable fitted behavior.
Dropout randomly masks activations during training to reduce co-adaptation.
Batch normalization normalizes intermediate activations using batch statistics and learned adjustments.
Validation evaluates held-out behavior without updating model weights.

Tensor shapes specify each dimension and must match operation requirements.
Tensor operations transform values, shapes or devices using defined broadcasting rules.
CPUs handle general computation; GPUs accelerate suitable parallel tensor workloads.
Automatic differentiation tracks operations to compute derivatives programmatically.
Autograd records a computational graph and computes gradients during backward.
Neural networks are built from modules with parameters and a forward method.
PyTorch loss modules compare predictions with targets in expected formats.
Optimizers update model parameters using their accumulated gradients.
A training loop loads batches, computes loss, backpropagates and updates parameters.
An evaluation loop disables gradient tracking and uses evaluation-mode behavior.

Loading restores model state into a compatible architecture and device.
GPU memory holds parameters, activations, gradients and temporary computation buffers.
Debugging training checks shapes, values, gradients, modes and tiny-data behavior.

Retrieval recall measures the fraction of relevant evidence retrieved.
Retrieval precision measures the fraction of retrieved evidence that is relevant.
Hallucination evaluation checks unsupported or false claims under a stated rubric.
Human evaluation collects expert or user judgments with clear guidance.
Automated evaluation computes repeatable metrics or model-based scores.

An LLM judge can score responses using a rubric, but can be biased, inconsistent and sensitive to ordering or style. Record judge configuration and sample human disagreements rather than treating one generated score as ground truth.

Regression evaluation repeats a fixed, versioned test set after prompt, model, tool or retrieval changes. Compare quality, cost and latency with a saved baseline and inspect the failing examples before accepting a change.
Prompt evaluation compares task outcomes under controlled prompt variants.
Agent evaluation measures task completion, action correctness and policy violations.
Trade-off analysis compares answer quality with cost and latency rather than one score.
10.5: Docker builds and runs applications as isolated containers from images.
VMs virtualize a full machine; containers share the host kernel.
An image is a layered package used as a template for containers.
A container is a running isolated process environment based on an image.
A Dockerfile declares reproducible image build instructions.
Building executes Dockerfile steps to produce a tagged image.
Running creates a container with chosen commands, mounts and limits.
Port mapping connects host endpoints to container network ports.
Volumes preserve data beyond a container's writable layer.
Container networks control connectivity and name resolution between services.
Compose defines a multi-container application and its local configuration.
Environment variables provide runtime configuration without rebuilding the image.
Multi-stage builds separate build tooling from the smaller runtime image.
Container security includes minimal images, non-root users, patched dependencies and limited privileges.

PaaS provides an application platform with more runtime operations managed for you.
SaaS provides a complete hosted application to end users.
Compute includes virtual machines, containers and functions executing workloads.
Storage services persist objects, blocks or file-like data.
Cloud networking connects resources through addresses, routes, subnets and access controls.

A virtual machine runs a guest operating system on virtualized hardware.
Serverless services manage execution capacity behind usage-based abstractions.
Container hosting runs packaged applications on a managed or self-operated platform.
GPU cloud services rent accelerator capacity with significant memory and cost constraints.
Environments separate development, testing, preview and production resources.
Cloud costs include compute, storage, requests, data transfer and idle capacity.
Disaster recovery uses tested backups and procedures to restore service after disruption.

Build pipelines transform checked source into reproducible deployable artifacts.
Automated tests run repeatable behavior checks without manual execution.
Deployment pipelines promote artifacts through controlled environments.

Release management coordinates versioning, approvals, rollout and communication.
Infrastructure as Code describes infrastructure through versioned declarative or scripted configuration.
Terraform plans and applies infrastructure changes through provider APIs.
Kubernetes orchestrates container workloads using declarative resources and reconciliation.
Container orchestration schedules workloads and manages networking, scaling and recovery.

Metrics summarize numerical behavior over time.
Traces connect timed operations across a request's execution path.
Observability is the ability to infer internal behavior from system outputs.
Monitoring tracks known signals and expected operating conditions.
Alerts notify operators when actionable conditions cross defined thresholds.
OpenTelemetry standardizes instrumentation and export of telemetry signals.

Performance monitoring measures latency, throughput and resource trends.

Incident response coordinates detection, mitigation, recovery and communication.

Performance monitoring compares predictions with outcomes when reliable labels become available.
Retraining pipelines regenerate candidates under controlled data and evaluation rules.

A context manager allocates relevant history and evidence within token limits.
A memory service stores controlled information for later retrieval or task continuity.

Monitoring observes known system health and performance signals.

Architecture diagrams show component boundaries, interactions and data flow.
An ADR records a decision, its context, alternatives and consequences.

Evaluation measures actual task performance on controlled examples.

Training changes parameters; inference computes outputs using the learned parameters.
Endpoints expose defined input and output contracts for inference.

Real-time inference responds within an interactive latency target.
GPU inference uses accelerators for suitable model computation.
Quantization represents values with fewer bits, trading precision for efficiency.

Distillation trains a smaller student to imitate a larger teacher's behavior.
Mixed precision combines numeric formats to improve speed or memory use.
KV caching reuses attention state from prior tokens during generation.
Continuous batching adds and removes requests dynamically as generation progresses.
Model throughput measures completed inference work or tokens per unit time.

11.5: Cost-performance decisions compare resource spending with measured workload outcomes.

During network partitions, stronger consistency can reduce request availability.
Complexity must earn its operational and maintenance cost through real requirements.

Caching improves reuse but requires a policy for stale data.

Build-versus-buy decisions compare control, integration effort, lifetime cost and vendor dependence.
6.7: Prompt engineering systematically changes instructions and context, then measures whether model behavior better satisfies a task. It does not update model weights.
System-level messages carry high-priority operating instructions in APIs that support this role. Exact role support and precedence vary by provider.
Developer instructions encode application rules and output expectations separately from a changing user request. Check the selected provider’s role contract.
A user message supplies a requested task and data. Content quoted inside it can be untrusted evidence rather than an instruction your application should execute.
Instruction hierarchy distinguishes trusted operating instructions from lower-trust requests and retrieved content. Enforce permissions in application code; model obedience is not access control.
A useful prompt separates the task, constraints, relevant context, examples and output contract so conflicting expectations can be spotted and tested.
A clear task specifies an observable result, allowed scope and success criteria. Replace subjective instructions with examples of acceptable and unacceptable behavior.
Useful context supplies relevant facts with source identity and boundaries. More context is not always better: irrelevant or conflicting evidence can reduce quality.
Few-shot prompting includes a small set of representative input/output examples. Choose diverse examples and keep evaluation cases separate from prompt examples.
Zero-shot prompting describes a task without demonstration examples. Establish this simple baseline before adding examples or a more complex workflow.
Structured output constrains response shape where a provider supports it. A valid schema does not guarantee factual correctness or safe actions.
Parse generated JSON and validate it against a runtime schema before using it. Handle missing fields, wrong types, unexpected values and invalid semantic content explicitly.
A code-managed prompt builder combines stable instructions with controlled inputs. Keep templates near the feature, with tests and code review; avoid copying one evolving string across services.
Prompt variables insert changing values through typed or validated inputs. Distinguish user-supplied data from trusted instructions and do not interpolate secrets into demonstrations.
Version prompt builders, fixtures and relevant model settings in source control. A meaningful experiment records which exact combination produced an output.
Reuse shared contracts and well-tested components while allowing task-specific instructions. One universal template often hides conflicting requirements.
Count compatible input tokens, reserve output capacity and select evidence within a budget. Truncating blindly can remove the instruction or source needed for a correct answer.
Context engineering decides what instructions, history, retrieved evidence, tool results and state reach a model at each step. Selection, provenance and access checks belong in the application.
Prompt injection attempts to turn untrusted text into instructions. Delimiters can clarify intent but do not replace authorization, restricted tools or checks on generated actions.
Test prompts on fixed normal, edge and adversarial inputs using explicit rubrics. Inspect both response content and any proposed tool operations.
Optimize against representative measurements, changing one major factor at a time. Compare quality, cost and latency rather than selecting the best-looking single answer.
A regression suite reruns fixed cases when prompts, models, retrieval or context assembly change. Track failures and uncertainty so a local improvement does not hide broader degradation.
